story.iWant: a managed Qdrant collection seeded with embeddings
story.soThat: semantic search is consistent across restarts
story.tasks: - Task 1: Implement Qdrant client wrapper (AC: #1) * Create src/jarvis/database/qdrant.py with connection management * Implement collection creation with 384-d vector config (Cosine distance) * Add error handling for connection failures * Add type hints and docstrings - Task 2: Create collection initialization script (AC: #1, #4) * Create initialization script (e.g., scripts/init_qdrant.py or CLI command) * Implement idempotent collection creation (check if exists first) * Configure collection parameters per architecture (HNSW, distance metric) * Add logging with structlog for initialization events - Task 3: Implement health check validation (AC: #2) * Add Qdrant health check to src/jarvis/cli/commands/doctor.py * Verify collection existence and configuration * Check vector dimensions and distance metric * Validate connection to Qdrant service - Task 4: Add persistence verification (AC: #3) * Verify volume mounting in docker-compose.yml (qdrant-data volume) * Test restart scenario (insert points → restart → verify points exist) * Document persistence configuration in comments - Task 5: Write unit and integration tests (AC: all) * Unit tests for Qdrant wrapper functions * Integration test: Initialize collection and verify structure * Integration test: Idempotency (run init twice, no errors) * Integration test: Persistence (restart Qdrant, verify data)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. Given embeddings exist in PostgreSQL staging tables, When the provisioning command runs, Then Qdrant collections with 384-d vectors and metadata payloads are created 2. Given the Qdrant service is running, When health checks are performed, Then they confirm replication parameters per architecture 3. Given a collection is initialized, When the system restarts, Then the collection persists with all data intact 4. Given the initialization script runs, When a collection already exists, Then the script handles idempotently without errors

doc.title: JARVIS System - Architecture Document
doc.snippet: Qdrant v1.15.5 (Vector Database): Purpose-built vector search engine. Native context sharding. Docker deployment with qdrant-client 1.15.1+. Collection configured with 384-d vectors (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), Cosine distance, HNSW config (m=16, ef_construct=200).

doc.title: JARVIS System - Architecture Document
doc.snippet: Collection "knowledge" with 384-dimension vectors, Cosine distance metric. Point structure includes vector + payload with text, source_file, section, domain, ingested_at. HNSW parameters: m=16, ef_construct=200, full_scan_threshold=10000.

doc.title: AI Advisor - Epic Breakdown
doc.snippet: As a vector engineer, I want a managed Qdrant collection seeded with embeddings, so that semantic search is consistent across restarts. Prerequisites: Story 2.2. Technical Notes: Use qdrant-client 1.15.1; maintain configuration file for distance metric (Cosine) and write operations.

doc.title: Qdrant Service Configuration
doc.snippet: Qdrant configured with HTTP port 6333, GRPC port 6334. Storage uses on_disk_payload: true, default_segment_number: 2. Log level: INFO.

artifact.reason: Establishes pattern for database connection management, environment-based configuration, and session factory. This story should follow the same pattern for Qdrant client initialization.
Custom exception hierarchy for database operations. Qdrant module should define similar exceptions (VectorDBError, QdrantConnectionError).
Health check command structure using Typer. Story should extend this with Qdrant-specific health checks via doctor_checks module.
Health check registry pattern. Add Qdrant collection verification check here (check_qdrant_collection function).
Established pattern for database dependency injection using get_session_factory(). Qdrant client should follow similar dependency pattern if exposed via API later.
Qdrant service already configured with volume persistence (qdrant-data:/qdrant/storage), port 6333 exposed, config file mounted. Story should verify this configuration.

package.name: sentence-transformers
package.comment: For embedding model - used in point payload

story-context.constraints: - Follow existing database module patterns from src/jarvis/database/postgres.py for connection management and error handling - Use pydantic-settings for Qdrant configuration (QDRANT_HOST, QDRANT_PORT environment variables with defaults) - Implement custom exception hierarchy (QdrantError, QdrantConnectionError, CollectionError) - Use structlog for all logging (logger.info, logger.error with structured context) - Follow Python 3.13+ type hints (use from __future__ import annotations) - All functions must have docstrings following Google style - Use snake_case for function names, PascalCase for classes, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constants - Collection name should be configurable but default to "knowledge" - Idempotent operations: check if collection exists before creating - Health checks must return structured results compatible with doctor_checks.summarize pattern - Volume persistence must be verified (qdrant-data volume already configured in docker-compose.yml) - Follow architecture.md HNSW config: m=16, ef_construct=200, full_scan_threshold=10000 - Distance metric: Cosine (per architecture.md) - Vector size: 384 dimensions (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model)

interface.name: QdrantClient
interface.signature: QdrantClient(host: str, port: int, timeout: float = 5.0)
interface.methods: - collection_exists(collection_name: str) -> bool - create_collection(collection_name: str, vectors_config: VectorParams, hnsw_config: HnswConfigDiff) -> bool - get_collection(collection_name: str) -> CollectionInfo - upsert(collection_name: str, points: List[PointStruct]) -> UpdateResult

interface.name: HnswConfigDiff
interface.signature: HnswConfigDiff(m: int, ef_construct: int, full_scan_threshold: int)

interface.name: get_session_factory pattern
interface.note: Follow postgres.py pattern - singleton client with lazy initialization

tests.standards: Follow existing test patterns from tests/integration/api/test_conversation_api_integration.py. Use pytest with type hints. Integration tests require Docker Compose (all services running). Unit tests should mock Qdrant client responses. Test file naming: test_*.py. Use fixtures for test setup (e.g., @pytest.fixture for qdrant_client). Follow pytest.ini_options: coverage tracking enabled, pythonpath includes src/. Test directory structure mirrors source (tests/unit/database/, tests/integration/database/).
tests.locations: - tests/unit/database/ - Unit tests with mocked Qdrant client - tests/integration/database/ - Integration tests requiring Docker - Create: tests/unit/database/test_qdrant.py - Create: tests/integration/database/test_qdrant_integration.py
tests.ideas:
AC #1 (Collection Creation): - Unit: Test collection creation with correct vector params (mock client.create_collection) - Unit: Test error handling when Qdrant connection fails - Integration: Create collection and verify it exists with correct config - Integration: Verify collection has 384-d vectors, Cosine distance, HNSW params
AC #2 (Health Checks): - Unit: Test health check returns structured result - Integration: Run jarvis doctor command and verify Qdrant check passes - Integration: Verify health check detects when Qdrant is down
AC #3 (Persistence): - Integration: Insert test points, restart Qdrant container, verify points still exist - Integration: Verify qdrant-data volume is mounted correctly
AC #4 (Idempotency): - Unit: Test collection_exists check before creation - Integration: Run init_collection twice, verify no errors on second run - Integration: Verify collection config unchanged after second init
